title: TB9-08461
frame:
Forum: Refugee Appeal Division (appeal tribunal).
Parties: the appellant and the Minister; names are redacted.
Decision under review (from the opening paragraphs): XXXX XXXX XXXX (the appellant) is appealing the decision of the Refugee Protection Division (RPD), which denies his claim for refugee protection.
How the layers nest here: The RAD member is the author (layer 1). The appellant and the Minister make submissions to the RAD (layer 2). The RPD decision under appeal is layer 3, and what the claimant or the Minister said to the RPD, as reported, is layer 4.

paragraphs.text: XXXX XXXX XXXX (the appellant) is appealing the decision of the Refugee Protection Division (RPD), which denies his claim for refugee protection.
He is a citizen of Nigeria. Determination
After conducting an independent analysis, I find that the RPD was incorrect in its finding that the appellant had a viable internal flight alternative (IFA). The appeal is therefore allowed.
I find that the Appellant is a Convention refugee. Allegations

In 2011, the appellant's wife died after a brief illness. He was left with three children and had difficulty providing and caring for them because of the loss of his wife. In August 2013, he met XXXX XXXX, a friend from secondary school, by chance. Mr. XXXX assisted him.

In September 2014, they started a sexual relationship. In XXXX 2014, their relationship was discovered by a neighbour. The appellant was taken to the traditional ruler, who decreed that he must undergo a ritual. The appellant escaped and lived near the Benin border. In XXXX 2016, he was recognized by a member of the community.
He planned to leave Nigeria with the assistance of his partner. In XXXX 2017, he entered the United States and then traveled to Canada in XXXX 2017, where he made a refugee claim.
The appellant alleges he cannot return to Nigeria, where his clan elders will persecute him for his sexual orientation (bisexual) and because he is XXXX XXXX. 1 The RPD decision

The RPD found that the appellant had a viable internal flight alternative and determined that his status as an individual who is XXXX XXXX did not make him a Convention refugee or person in need of protection. My role as a member of the RAD
The standard of review is correctness.2 I am required to conduct an independent assessment and not defer to the RPD except in limited circumstance, which do not arise in this case.
I have considered the SOGIE guidelines.
The appellant is not submitting new evidence. Nor is he requesting an oral hearing.3 The appellant is a Convention refugee

While the RPD did not make an explicit finding with respect to the appellant's sexual orientation, it did accept that the appellant had a same-sex relationship with a friend.4 The appellant's oral evidence was deemed credible by the RPD. The panel did not ask any questions about supporting documentation, such as a letter from the appellant's lover.
The RPD acknowledges that the sexual relations between individuals of the same sex are illegal.

Therefore, an IFA is unreasonable. While it is true that the government authorities and the public are unaware of the appellant's sexual orientation in the IFA, it would mean that he would have to hide his sexual orientation. While he may choose to do so, this cannot be an expectation on part of the RPD or the RAD.
As same-sex activity is illegal, the appellant has rebutted the presumption of state protection. Nor is there a viable IFA as same-sex activity is illegal throughout Nigeria.

For these reasons, I allow the appeal and find that the appellant is a Convention refugee, based on his membership in a particular social group (individuals with non-heterosexual sexual orientations). This is an innate characteristic.
I will not go on to consider his profile as an individual XXXX XXXX as I find that he is a Convention refugee based on his sexual orientation. Conlusion

The appeal is allowed. I set aside the determination of the RPD and substitute my own determination that the appellant is a Convention refugee. (signed) "R. Seyan" R.
